---

## Incident Report: Malware Infection via Fake FedEx Phishing Page

**Capture:** `2024-08-15-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (SHA256 `e154de6895c5f0a9edd07b1279b33014507236dbb44a449790c255b87a327a3c`), 18,189 packets, 2024-08-15 04:09:43 – 04:42:26 UTC (1962s duration). No separate IDS/Suricata alert file was present in the evidence directory; all findings below are derived directly from packet analysis with tshark.

### 1. Victim host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.8.15.133** |
| MAC address | **00:1c:bf:03:54:82** (Intel NIC) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-H8ALZBV** |
| Windows domain | LAFONTAINEBLEU (lafontainebleu.org, DC at 10.8.15.4 / WIN-JEGJIX7Q9RS) |
| Logged-in user | **plucero** |

Confirmed via DHCP option 12 (hostname), NBNS name registrations, ARP-to-MAC binding, and Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ CNameString fields (both `DESKTOP-H8ALZBV$` machine account and `plucero` user principal authenticating from 10.8.15.133 against the DC at 10.8.15.4).

### 2. Malware family
**Latrodectus** (loader/downloader malware, IcedID-lineage). **Attribution basis: behavioral, not signature-confirmed** — no local IDS/Suricata alert artifact was provided in this evidence set, so this identification rests on the observed infection chain and network fingerprints rather than a rule hit:
- Fake-invoice phishing lure serving a ZIP with a heavily junk-padded `.js` downloader (7 MB file, ~99% inert scraped filler text with a small embedded payload) — a known Latrodectus AV-evasion technique.
- Follow-on BITS-based (`Microsoft BITS/7.8` user-agent) retrieval of a PE32+ DLL from a bare IP address (no DNS lookup preceded it).
- Persistent post-infection HTTP beaconing to that same IP with a malformed, spaced user-agent string `Mozilla / 5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)` and an encrypted blob carried in the `Cookie:` header on every request — a distinctive, previously-documented Latrodectus C2 fingerprint.

### 3. Indicators of compromise (all observed directly in the capture)

**Delivery domains (phishing lure, fake FedEx):**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` → resolved to 104.21.55.70 / 172.67.170.159 (Cloudflare-fronted)
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` → resolved to 172.67.170.159 / 104.21.55.70

**Malicious URL:**
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` (GET, t=63.9s) → returned `application/octet-stream` ZIP archive.

**Command-and-control endpoint:**
- **72.5.43.29:80/tcp** (plain HTTP, contacted directly by IP — no A-record lookup ever seen for it). BITS download at t≈136s; persistent GET/POST `/` beacon every ~5–10s from t≈197s through the end of the capture at t≈1962s (encrypted Cookie header + encrypted POST body, `400 Bad Request` echoed back each time).

**Files transferred / SHA256 hashes:**
| File | SHA256 | Context |
|---|---|---|
| ZIP archive (`managements?...` response) | `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5` | Delivered from quote.checkfedexexp.com |
| `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` | `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c` | JS downloader inside the ZIP, junk-padded to ~7 MB |
| `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (PE32+ DLL) | `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` | Second-stage payload, pulled via `Microsoft BITS/7.8` from `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` at t≈136s; this is the loaded C2 module |

**Note on excluded items:** the capture also contains a `TeamViewer` installer, `Teamviewer_Resource_fr` DLL, and `am_delta_patch...exe`, but these were all served over HTTP by `199.232.210.172` (`msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com`), Microsoft's legitimate Delivery Optimization CDN, fetched via `Microsoft BITS/7.8` — this is routine Windows Update/enterprise software delivery traffic, not part of the infection chain, and is not listed as an IOC.

### Summary
User `plucero` on `DESKTOP-H8ALZBV` (10.8.15.133) visited a fake FedEx-themed phishing site (`quote.checkfedexexp.com` / `business.checkfedexexp.com`) and downloaded a ZIP containing an obfuscated JScript downloader. That script pulled a DLL payload via a BITS job from `72.5.43.29`, which then established continuous encrypted HTTP beaconing back to `72.5.43.29:80` for the remainder of the capture — consistent with a Latrodectus loader infection.
